why: What the analysis pass looks for in a message body. Two of these are syntax — an HTML tag, a run of whitespace, a URL — and two are vocabulary that grows: the currencies this fleet is billed in, and the way English mail writes a date. The vocabulary is the reason this is a file rather than five regexes in the source: adding a currency is adding a word to a record, and the record says which currencies were chosen and why the date shapes stop where they do.
tag_why: An HTML element, removed before the body is read as text.
space_why: Any run of whitespace, collapsed to one so a flattened body reads as sentences.
url_why: A link, ended at the characters that cannot appear inside one in mail: quotes, angle brackets, a closing paren or bracket.
amount_why: A sum of money, written code-first, symbol-first or code-last. The four currencies are the ones this fleet is actually billed in — dollars for the clouds, euros and pounds for the European hosts, złoty for the Polish invoices. A currency nobody bills us in would only add false positives.
date_why: A date as mail writes it: ISO, or an English month with a day and an optional year. Only this century, because a four-digit year that is not 20xx in a billing mail is a version number or an order reference far more often than a date.
